key_claims.claim: Prenatal ultrasound features of closed spinal dysraphism subtypes can be systematically characterized and linked to functional outcomes at 18 and 36 months, enabling subtype-specific prognostication.

After PGT-A euploid embryo transfer, cfDNA screening has a positive predictive value of only 12.5% for aneuploidy, residual aneuploidy risk is 0.1%, and chromosomal microarray adds 0.5% clinically relevant findings.
A structured counseling framework for fetal intracranial hemorrhage can be built from current evidence on etiology, genetic workup, and neurodevelopmental outcomes.
External validation of 10 sagittal aortic-arch parameters plus a new multivariable model improves prenatal discrimination for coarctation of the aorta.
Isolated narrow cavum septi pellucidi normalizes in 58% of fetuses by late second trimester, and 81.5% of infants have normal neurodevelopment at 2 years.
